entries.notes: Full n5 x 200-step replay of the stored sampler tape, nothing sliced; triangle attention on the port's own default (cueq_jit, recorded in the tripwire), confidence heads off. Sample 1 is excluded because it is the reduction-order-sensitive one: the panel measured it at 0.172 A with non-deterministic XLA reductions and 0.016 A with --xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true (docs/protenix-master-panel-2026-09-09.md:126-135, where it is 1-based 'sample 2'), and on CPU it lands at 0.1132 A, twice any other sample. Sample 3 is excluded because the two native processes are themselves 0.0946 A apart there (native-A-vs-native-B.json), so an assertion on it measures upstream chaos rather than this port. Detection floor, measured rather than argued: swapping one row of one MSA cycle -- one row of 160, in one cycle of ten -- moves the asserted samples to 0.0171 / 0.0419 / 0.1387 A, so sample 4 crosses this tolerance at 2.3x and the shipped negative-control test catches it; the same perturbation is invisible at Tier A. What this tier does NOT catch is a single initial-noise element: adding 1.0 to one of the 9,030 values in init_noise moved sample 0 by 4.9e-6 A and left the other four bitwise, because the sampler contracts toward its trajectory rather than amplifying that draw. Against the coordinate scale the GPU panel works at, this tier is coarse: CPU XLA already sits 0.015-0.051 A from the GPU native run, so a regression has to push an asserted sample past 0.06 A -- 0.045 A of headroom on samples 0 and 2, 0.009 A on sample 4 -- and the panel's own 0.037 A port-vs-native maximum is below that. prediction.npz ships whole (16 MB) although only its `coordinate` array is read: a derived 36 KB file would hash to nothing in any capture and `python -m tests.parity.fetch` could never find it. Fetch with `--from /home/jaemin/non-project/optimizing/foldjax-bench/protenix-master-native-20260909-9yET4f/protein_1ubq` (the case directory), because foldjax-input.npz lives in port-A and the rest in native-A.
